Ming@tslaming · Nov 26

Tslaming video: Elon admitted SpaceX is not yet on the podium for digital superintelligence; the post compares Grok to the top three AIs (628 likes).

Earlier this month, SpaceX caught a Starship falling back from orbit with the arms of the tower that launched it, a first in history 🚀

Yet @elonmusk just admitted he's sad, because SpaceX's AI isn't even in the world's top three 😢

That's quite a confession from the guy who builds the biggest rocket on Earth.

So who's beating SpaceX, and what's Elon doing about it?

🥉 The top three AIs score around 60, and Grok scores 35

"Digital superintelligence" is Elon's name for AI that can outthink humans. SpaceX has been chasing it since February, when it bought xAI, the maker of Grok.

The scoreboard everyone watches comes from Artificial Analysis, an independent tester that hits every major AI with the same brutal exams in science, coding, and real-world work.

On a board like that, Elon's "podium" means the top three AI companies, like gold, silver, and bronze at the Olympics. Right now those medals go to Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google, with their best models scoring around 60 to 65.

Grok 4.7, the Grok anyone can use today, scores about 35, which puts it outside the top ten.

Elon wasn't being modest.

🛠️ Elon's catch-up plan runs on Starlink code and 770,000 GPUs

This gap isn't news to Elon. On November 10, he called Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 "a masterpiece" and admitted the next Grok won't match it. Grok 4.8 and Grok 5 are how SpaceX plans to close in.

Grok 4.8 comes first. It's a 2.5 trillion parameter model, which means it has 2.5 trillion tiny dials it adjusts while learning, and Elon promises it will "bear no resemblance" to Grok 4.7.

To build it, the team did something very SpaceX. They dumped the standard AI tools and rewrote the software that trains and runs Grok from scratch in C and C++, based on work by the engineers who built Starlink.

Elon proudly pointed out that SpaceX writes its own headers and calculates its own time, leap seconds included.

All that rewriting is part of why Grok 4.8 is late. He says its test scores are starting to climb, and for now it's only running in trials behind the scenes.

Then comes the heavyweight. Elon has put Grok 5 at about 6 trillion parameters, more than twice the size of Grok 4.8. It's training on Colossus 2 in Memphis, a monster that held about 770,000 NVIDIA GPUs at the end of October, by his count.

Grok 5 is the one Elon expects to pass Opus 5.5, maybe within two or three months, "with continued acceleration thereafter."

🚀 Why the sad emoji is bullish: SpaceX plans to put AI in orbit

Elon could have answered with a rocket victory lap. He called out his own AI in public instead, and that sad emoji reads like a promise to fix it.

Climbing that scoreboard takes more compute, and SpaceX itself says its AI progress is driven by compute. Compute runs on electricity, and lots of it. Colossus 2 already needs its own gas turbines, backed by more than a thousand Tesla Megapacks, by analysts' count.

And Elon is thinking way bigger than Memphis. He has said the world adds roughly 20 gigawatts of AI computing a year, about 2% of what his companies will eventually need, and he projects on the order of a terawatt, or 1,000 gigawatts, for AI satellites in space.

Starmind is how SpaceX plans to get there. Each satellite is an AI computer powered by nonstop sunlight in space, and the satellites talk to each other with lasers. This week, the FCC cleared SpaceX to launch up to 1 million of them, with the first due by 2033 and the full fleet by 2040.

That could give Grok room to grow far beyond anything one city's power supply can handle.

Elon may be sad about today's scoreboard. But the rocket that landed in that tower's arms was built to fly again and again so launches get cheaper, and it's expected to carry those satellites to orbit.

Not one lab on the podium owns a rocket.

James Delotis: Morning AI News Nov 27 says Anthropic rewrote the Claude Messages API in Rust with Claude agents: about 70% lower CPU per request and 20% faster median time-to-first-token (image post) (0 likes).

AI & Tech Daily@JamesDelotis
Morning AI News
November 27, 2026

Lab & product updates
- **Anthropic** rewrote its Claude Messages API in Rust using Claude agents for most of the work. The company reports roughly 70% lower CPU per request and a 20% faster median time-to-first-token, with no downtime. Verification of the rewrite was the harder part than the code generation.
- **OpenAI** fixed a billing error that had been incorrectly discounting GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage. After the fix, users hit limits about 40% faster on Astra and 25% faster on Sol than last week. Eligible subscribers get an extra usage reset; Business users get free Fast Mode through the end of 2026. OpenAI is also testing a combined Chat + Work experience with shared limits.
- **Google** set a hard date: Workspace agents must use MCP (instead of calling Workspace REST APIs directly) starting February 1, 2027. Scaled-tier billing for that begins April 1, 2027.
- **Neuralink** received FDA approval for a pivotal U.S. trial of its brain-computer interface in people with severe paralysis from ALS.

Policy, finance & supply chain
- The **Bank of England** warned that AI-related financing is becoming more interconnected and opaque, raising the risk that stress spreads across markets. It flagged hyperscaler exposure (including debt, leases, and purchase agreements) above $4 trillion.
- **Nvidia** has told partners (including Dell and Supermicro) to halt AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia as tighter U.S. export rules take effect.
- U.S. chip restrictions and distillation limits are reportedly delaying Chinese models. Z.ai’s GLM-5.5 has slipped to Q1 2027 or later; Moonshot and others face longer gaps between major releases.
- A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to block Character.AI from selling user chat histories as part of its Chapter 11 process (more than 21 million U.S. accounts involved, including many belonging to minors).

Other notes
- **Canada** expanded its AI Compute Access Fund with a $700 million top-up, bringing the total to $1 billion, and opened a new health and life sciences call.
- **Tencent** open-sourced DFly2, a speculative decoding tool that reportedly boosts throughput for models like DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash by up to 81% at long context.
- Oregon and Virginia AGs sued SpaceX (and related Musk companies) over Grok-generated deepfakes, citing inadequate safeguards against sexualized imagery of real people.
- A new Lean 4 formalization of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis appeared on GitHub and quickly gained attention.
